title: Collection-Service Fees Counted in the Patient Financial Assistance Program Laboratory-Payments Deduction
content:
**Rule.** For a case under the Patient Financial Assistance Program, collection fees counted are added to the laboratory-payments deduction before it is rounded, by the household's collection history in Specimen Collection Appointments: a household with a Medicare homebound certification on a collection visit adds every collection-service fee it paid within the deduction window; a household that paid a home-visit trip fee within the deduction window adds the trip, additional-patient and weekend fees it paid within the window, but not cancellation or no-show fees; any other household adds no collection fees.

The amount is added to the laboratory-payments deduction itself, after the percent of the payments counted has been taken and before the deduction is rounded to the cent.

## Fee table

| Fee paid within the deduction window | Household with a Medicare homebound certification on a collection visit | Household without that certification that paid a home-visit trip fee within the window | Any other household |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trip fee | Added | Added | Not added |
| Additional-patient fee | Added | Added | Not added |
| Weekend surcharge | Added | Added | Not added |
| Late-cancellation fee | Added | Not added | Not added |
| No-show fee | Added | Not added | Not added |

## Worked figures (hypothetical households; fees paid within the deduction window)

Fees paid: trip fee $45.00, additional-patient fee $20.00, weekend surcharge $15.00, no-show fee $25.00.

- With a Medicare homebound certification on a collection visit: $105.00 is added, every fee paid.
- Without that certification: the trip fee was paid within the window, so $80.00 is added (trip, additional-patient and weekend fees); the no-show fee is not added.
- A household that paid only a no-show fee of $25.00 within the window, with no certification and no trip fee: nothing is added.
